change: Run existing String search and bracket scanning directly on owned buffers, then release their borrows before constructing the result.

contract.before: Clone the receiver and search needle, or the bracket-scan input; compute a scalar result; call the current Integer constructor.
contract.after: Perform the same owner representation checks and pure scan under a private buffer borrow; carry only the scalar result out of the borrow and call the same constructor.
preserved: Receiver validation precedes empty-needle matching. A non-String needle still answers nil.
Search remains byte-oriented, including binary bytes, and returns the same first match.
The existing bracket scanner and its quoted-string/comment/escape rules are unchanged.
No private borrow spans the current Integer constructor or GC.
Dependency-context access, result identities, errors and Id semantics are unchanged.

microbenchmark.scope: Existing indexOf: and bracketDepth through Id, input sizes 64 bytes/4 KiB/1 MiB. Early match, empty needle, absent needle, and bracket-free scan. Serial ABBA, five samples/process. Automatic GC disabled only for timed work; precise GC outside samples. Results checked.

validation: Expanded String/Error test: binary search, empty needle, missing/invalid needle, quoted/escaped/commented brackets, receiver-error precedence, and GC during current result construction.
Full Oop core/compiler/GC and negative dispatch/construction contracts.
limits: The large gain is early-match/empty-needle search on large Strings. Full misses and bracket scans remain dominated by scanning and show no clear speedup.
Microbenchmark timing excludes explicit GC and uses disabled automatic GC for bounded timed work; runtime policy is unchanged.
Only String differs between prefixes. The installed user runtime was not replaced.
